answer.rationale:
The competitor's entry pricing creates pressure to reach for promotional_pricing, and memory_73 is the loudest revenue number in the inherited record (+31% trials, +18% quarterly revenue). But that record is exactly where I most distrust the summary: it reports trial starts and quarterly revenue for small accounts over a 12-week window with standard reporting cadence, which is short enough that retention, renewal, and margin effects on discount-acquired accounts would not yet have surfaced. Discount-led acquisition is the classic case where the measured metric moves and the objective (sustainable long-term qualified revenue) moves the other way, and it would also concede price framing to the competitor. So I want the original record for memory_73 specifically to see whether retention/LTV of discounted cohorts was ever measured or whether the summary silently converted a short-run revenue bump into a durable win.

The two metrics actually deteriorating are activation (-6%) and onboarding completion (-4%), and three inherited memories point at that surface: memory_31 (fewer required fields lifted SMB first-week activation, described as durable), memory_86 (shorter onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value), memory_91 (in-product activation messaging lifted week-one engagement). These address the observed decline directly rather than buying volume around it, and they plausibly also blunt the competitor by improving time-to-value for the same price-sensitive SMB segment that is churning to cheap alternatives. I verify memory_86 as the second pull because it is the one my intended action leans on most heavily and its summary stops at completion and adoption \u2014 upstream funnel metrics \u2014 without connecting to qualified revenue; I want to know whether completion lift ever translated downstream or merely moved accounts faster through a step.

I am deliberately not verifying memory_57 or memory_44: referral incentives depend on an established-customer base that is currently under competitive pressure, and enterprise sales-assist does not touch the SMB segment where the decline is concentrated. Neither is my leading candidate this week.

Intent is simplify_onboarding at standard experiment scale, not broad rollout: the inherited evidence is a summary of a prior context, the current quarter's conditions differ (active competitor, declining baseline), and memory_31's claim of durability is asserted rather than shown. I hold this intent loosely \u2014 if the memory_86 record shows the completion lift never reached revenue, I would shift to activation_messaging (memory_91) as the closer match to the larger -6% activation gap; if the memory_73 record unexpectedly shows measured retention holding past the 12-week window, promotional_pricing becomes defensible as a small_guarded_test with explicit cohort-retention instrumentation, but not otherwise.
